doctrine: AI video production shifts from prompt-and-pray to controlled pipeline management. The operator advantage comes from: (1) Character consistency first: train Soul ID with 20-30 reference photos (varied angles/lighting) to avoid 'AI inconsistency tax'. (2) Build shot library before animating: run master image through Shots app (1 image = 9 unique angles), decoupling identity from appearance via Outfit Swap. (3) Sequential production pipeline: pre-production (character definition + keyframes + prop sheets) > production (scene keyframes + animation + cinema studio camera simulation) > post-production (review + upscale + export). (4) Prompt architecture requires shot structure declaration (at top of every prompt): shots, duration, aspect ratio, then reference tags (character vs style), camera behavior (what IS doing and NOT doing), negative constraints. Seedance format recipes (Transformations highest-performing, Orbs first-person POV, POVs locked perspective, Fights choreographed, Animation stylized) have specific formulas. (5) Models selection: WAN 2.6 for cinematic continuity/narrative, Kling 2.6/3.0 for dialogue/lip-sync, Seedance 2.0 for animation/action/viral, Minimax Hailuo 02 for rapid iteration. (6) Monetization: Higgsfield Earn pays per post (3 posts/day outperforms 1 post/week); real money in services: AI influencer agency, brand kits, cinematic B-roll packs, prompt packs, recurring video series. Position as 'studio-in-a-box' and virtual production, not random prompting. (7) The leverage principle: compound asset reuse. One character, nine angles, five outfits, three animation styles, twenty clips = one month of content. Consistency assets + reusable libraries are the operating advantage.

Seedance Fights: Exact choreography beat by beat. Include slow-motion ramps: RAMPS TO SLOW MOTION / SNAPS BACK.
Seedance Animation: Break 15s into timed blocks. Keyframe as style reference. Describe physics precisely.
